chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ibn Faddal from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The judgment is two judgments: the judgment of Allah and the judgment of ignorance.
And Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who have certainty?'
And I bear witness against Zayd ibn Thabit that he indeed judged in the inheritances with the judgment of ignorance.

key_terms.زَيْدُ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ: Zayd ibn Thabit, a companion of the Prophet
key_terms.لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ: For a people who have certainty

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between hukm Allah and hukm al-jahiliyyah according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) contrasts divine judgment with the judgment of pre-Islamic ignorance, citing the Quranic verse that praises Allah's judgment. He then provides a specific historical example, testifying that Zayd ibn Thabit, a prominent companion, judged in matters of inheritance using the judgment of ignorance rather than divine law.
